subject: HarborTech private cluster: capacity profiles, IO guardrails, and preflight asks
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@harbortech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: TopCloud Solutions <procurement@topcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff and a few sizing questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick intro call last week. We started pulling together the site inventory and an initial workload summary (attached). Before we schedule a hands-on preflight, a few open items from our side that will determine node/storage profiles:

- Typical inference QPS (steady vs peak) — we have rough numbers in the PDF but would like your recommendation on how to size for 99th percentile.
- Local cache behavior: some of our feature stores will benefit from NVMe-local KV cache; need guidance on crash/snapshot expectations.
- Model artifacts: how we should carve fast vs cold storage for model checkpoints (we run a model registry that keeps frequent pulls).
- Network: no egress outside our VPC; we can do VPC peering to your control plane but want to avoid cross-tenant NAT.

I've attached site-inventory.xlsx and redacted_workload_summary.pdf. Can you share a short checklist you want filled before we run the workshop? Also looping procurement to confirm any paperwork.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director, Cloud Ops
HarborTech

Attachments: site-inventory.xlsx (xlsx), redacted_workload_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@harbortech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, TopCloud Solutions <procurement@topcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff and a few sizing questions

Thanks Elena — attached PDF looked good on first pass. High level checklist and our preflight asks below so the workshop is efficient:

Preflight checklist (what we'd like from HarborTech ahead of the workshop):
1) Workload CSV: per-service expected steady QPS and peak QPS, median and 99th perc. (one-line per service) — you already have this but a plain CSV helps our sizing scripts.
2) Network diagram: VPC/subnet CIDRs, peering routes, egress policies, and any customer-managed firewalls.
3) Storage SLA: RPO/RTO expectations for model artifacts and ephemeral caches.
4) Compliance constraints: SOC2 or any data residency rules (call these out).
5) Access: a service account or temporary IAM role we can use in the workshop for read-only inventory pulls.

Initial recommendations to consider now (we'll refine during the workshop):
- Control plane: 3 small dedicated VMs (HA), prefer isolated management network with no external NAT.
- Node pools: create separate pools for inference-gpu, batch-cpu, and infra/sidecar workloads. Keep the inference-gpu pool slim to reduce cold-start interference.
- Disk tiers: local NVMe for token/KV cache and hot model shards; a cluster-level fast-backend (Ceph/RBD or local LVM on NVMe) for ephemeral inference scratch; an object-store-backed archive for checkpoints.
- IO guardrails: set eviction thresholds and node-local device pressure watchers; we recommend enforced pod-level disk quotas for scratch mounts.

Next steps: Marissa and Laura, can you confirm availability for a 90-min workshop (remote) next week? Elena, if you can drop the CSV and network diagram into the Drive link I shared, we will run sizing ahead of time.

Cheers,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HarborTech private cluster: capacity profiles, IO guardrails, and preflight asks

Karthik — quick internal note before the workshop. Based on the PDF:

- Baseline sizing idea (scratch calculations): if HarborTech steady inference QPS is ~1200 across 8 services with 95% on short prompts, target 4 inference nodes (A100-80GB equivalent) for baseline, with burst pool for spikes. Add 1-2 nodes for redundancy depending on desired headroom.
- Local NVMe usage: recommend a single NVMe per GPU node (2-4 TB) mounted as ephemeral scratch for KV cache; run a nightly checkpoint sync to cluster archive.
- Storage classes: define sc-fast (local NVMe RWX for pods that need low latency), sc-block (RBD for short-lived artifacts), sc-archive (S3-compatible object store for long-term checkpoints).
- Network constraints: since no public egress, build a private S3 gateway in the customer VPC for model pulls and backups. Avoid internet-facing control-plane components; use peering and restricted ports.

I'll draft a slide with concrete pod/volume limits and eviction thresholds (pod ephemeral-storage: request/limit patterns) and upload before the call. Also propose a 90-min agenda: intake review (20m), sizing run (30m), storage and network guardrails (30m), next steps and action list (10m).

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik/Marissa — this is helpful. We can deliver the CSV and the network diagram today; I'll also surface the compliance matrix (SOC2 scoped) and add the procurement contact in a follow-up. A couple clarifications that matter for sizing:

- We cannot use any public managed object store; we will run an S3-compatible gateway inside our VPC (TopCloud will provision).
- Desired RPO for model artifacts is 12 hours, RTO for core inference services is 60 minutes.
- Peak QPS for a single service can spike to ~600 QPS for 3-4 minutes during batch imports.

I'll upload the CSV and diagrams to the Drive link and confirm the TopCloud contact. Workshop availability: Thursday 10/22 10:00–11:30 PT works for our ops and procurement folks.

Elena
Director, Cloud Ops
HarborTech

summary: Preflight thread with HarborTech to align on private Kubernetes deployment sizing, node pool separation, NVMe use for KV cache, storage-class recommendations, and a 90-min workshop to finalize capacity and network guardrails.
